g.text: Docker Desktop: how traffic leaves, and how published ports come in
Both directions go through a host-side process; the VM itself is never directly addressable from outside.
Outbound: a container reaches the Internet
The host process opens ordinary TCP/IP sockets, so firewalls, VPNs and proxies see traffic coming from IT, not from a VM.
Inbound: a published port (docker run -p 8080:80 nginx)
Documented: this path exists for PUBLISHED container ports. Whether the same mechanism can expose the Engine's own ports (2377, 7946, 4789) to other
machines is not documented, and is the open question of the next diagram.
